_about: Teodor's subject library, short form. Layer 1: subjects.<id>; layer 2: styles.<style>.<id>. Docs: docs/subjects/README.md.

hair.summary: A mass of fibres on the skull, grouped into locks; shines in a band across the strands that follows the skull.

primary_highlight.value: colour of the light, shifted 5-10 deg toward the root

secondary_highlight.value: hair-coloured, shifted toward the tip; absent in black hair

backlight.value: light hair glows strongly when lit from behind

curl_types.value: 8, by curve diameter, curl index, number of waves

wet.value: darker (wetting roughly halves albedo of rough matte surfaces, e.g. sand 0.18 -> 0.09); clumped, flat to skull

checks: Squint: one mass, 3-7 big light/shadow shapes, silhouette wider than the skull
Highlight runs across the strands and curves with the skull; light-coloured, with a narrower hair-coloured band on the tip side
No strands or texture inside shadow shapes; strands only in light and at the silhouette
Hairline graded into skin, never outlined; hair casts shadow on forehead/neck
Gravity and wind agree with cloth, smoke and trees
Each person's hair differs in type, colour, length and mass

drapery.summary: Cloth hangs from support points, folds where pushed or pulled, wraps the body; material sets fold size; wind and water change it.

support_points.value: shoulders, collarbones, chest, hips, elbows, knees, buttocks, seams, waistbands, garment edges

gravity.value: free cloth falls straight down between support points; widest part of a two-point fold at its midpoint

fold_types.source: Bridgman, Drawing the Draped Figure; Proko; Pluralsight

material.value: thick/stiff: few large straight-edged folds; silk/satin: many narrow clinging folds; wool/fur: large gentle contours; velvet: single soft folds

body_reveal.value: body shows at tension points and where wind presses thin cloth; hidden between
body_reveal.source: Leonardo Notebooks 391; Met (wet drapery); tension-point reading is judgement

wind.value: windward side clings, leeward billows as flag folds, free edges flutter in smaller waves; heavy cloth barely lifts

wet.value: darker, heavier, clings, fewer deeper folds, thin cloth translucent
wet.source: Lekner & Dorf 1988 for darkening; rest judgement

hierarchy.value: 1-2 dominant fold systems per garment section; small wrinkles only at compressions

checks: Every main fold starts at a support point, compression or pull; free cloth falls plumb unless wind redirects it
Fold size matches the material
Hems, cuffs, seams and stripes wrap the body as ellipses/cross-contours
Folds painted as forms with light and shadow planes, not lines; creases hard, rolls soft
Body shows at tension points, hidden between
Small wrinkles only at compressions; large quiet areas elsewhere
Wind, hair and cloth agree in direction and strength
avoid: dark lines drawn over flat colour
one fabric behaviour for all materials

crowd.summary: Mostly small groups spaced by relationship and density, heads on the viewer's eye level, read as a whole first, individuals by a few characters.

walking_shapes.value: abreast at low density; V (3) and U (4) bent forward at higher density

standing_groups.value: F-formations around an empty shared space: vis-a-vis, L, side-by-side, circle

density_per_m2.value: ~1 loose; 2 event safety assessment; 4 moving queue; 4.7 Green Guide standing; 5 upper limit; 6-10 crush

eye_level.value: on flat ground, standing viewer: all adult heads on the horizon; seated viewer: near heads well above it

detail_gradient.value: faces/hands near; heads, posture, colour middle; silhouettes far

perception.value: viewers extract mean emotion, gaze, identity of a crowd at a glance

checks: Eye level fixed; standing adult heads on the same ground sit on it; exceptions explained
Built of groups (mostly 2-4) spaced by relationship, facing each other or a shared focus; no grid, not all frontal
Figure size falls consistently with distance (check against a door)
Detail falls off with depth
A few characters differ clearly from the average; no two neighbours share a pose
Contact and cast shadows tie every figure down; edges between figures partly lost
Squint: one designed value mass with a broken top edge
avoid: floating heads off the eye level
detail everywhere or an empty block

light-shadow.summary: Two families split at the terminator; shadows coloured by what lights them; cast-shadow edges set by source size; contrast decays with distance through air.

values_0_10.source: Proko, Elements of Light and Shadow

family_rule.value: darkest light-side value lighter than lightest shadow-side value; reflected light below darkest halftone

core_shadow.value: exists because the key is stronger than the bounce; two equal opposite lights remove it

penumbra.value: about 1/110 of casting distance in sunlight (1 cm at 1 m)

light_from_above_prior.value: above, slightly left: ~3 deg (O'Shea 2010 fit) to ~20 deg left in other studies

shadow_colour.value: colour of what lights the shadow: blue skylight outdoors in sun, warm if warm reflectors and blocked sky

aerial_contrast.value: contrast ~ 0.02^(d/V) for visibility V: 38% at V/4, 14% at V/2; haze V 2-5 km, fog <1 km

aerial_colour.value: distant darks turn bluest; five times as far, five times bluer

checks: Key light named (direction, size, colour) and the fill named; all terminators and cast shadows agree
Squint/notan: two clear families, no overlap
Each form has core shadow, reflected light inside the shadow, occlusion at contacts
Cast shadows sharp at contact, softer with distance and with bigger sources
Shadow colour from the fill and nearby reflectors, not a fixed complement
With distance, contrast and saturation fall toward the air's colour, darks first
Highlights only on glossy or wet surfaces, in the light's colour, few
avoid: reflected light as bright as halftones
decorative rim light without a source

space.summary: Central projection from one eye: horizon = eye level, parallels share a vanishing point, size ~ 1/distance; depth read from overlap, size, height on the ground plane and, far away, aerial perspective.

key_numbers.image_size: z = Z * x / X (object size Z at distance X, viewing distance x) (handprint)
key_numbers.two_point_vp: VPs 90 deg apart; each at tan(angle) * viewing distance from centre of vision; 45/45 -> VPs two viewing distances apart; 30/60 -> 0.58 and 1.73 (handprint)
key_numbers.three_point_vp: distance of VP3 from horizon >= distance between VPL and VPR (OUP)
key_numbers.ground_interval_compression: image height of a ground step ~ f*h*dD/D^2 (geometry, computed)
key_numbers.aerial: C = C0*exp(-sigma*d); visual range = 3.912/sigma; fog <1 km, mist 1-2 km, haze 2-5 km; scene.py fog density 0.008 ~ 490 m range (fog), 0.0013 ~ 3 km haze, 0.0002 ~ 20 km clear (computed)

depth_cue_ranges_m.vista: >30: occlusion, height in field, size, aerial perspective

key_numbers.sun_shadow_penumbra: about 1% of distance from casting edge (sun 0.5 deg)

rules: One horizon; all horizontal parallels vanish on it; standing figures of equal height on flat ground are cut by it at the same place (geometry, handprint)
Keep VPs far apart; too close makes boxes bulge (handprint)
Verticals all vertical (level gaze) or all converge on one third VP (handprint, OUP)
Inclined planes vanish on auxiliary VPs on the vertical through the VP of their horizontal direction (OUP)
Ellipse minor axis on the cylinder axis; rounder away from eye level; no pointed ends (NMA, BYU)
Perspective comes from viewer position, not lens: close = extension, far = compression (Wikipedia, Perspective distortion)
Aerial perspective: contrast falls first, darks lighten and lights dim toward the horizon-sky value and hue; weather sets the rate (Koschmieder)
Sun shadows converge on one point on the horizon (perspective notes)
checks: one horizon; figures' eyes keyed to it by camera eye height
fov chosen on purpose; key forms inside central 60 deg
equal ground intervals shrink ~1/D^2
clear overlap (no tangents) at each depth step
darks lift and contrast shrinks step by step toward the horizon, at a rate fitting the stated weather
all sun shadows converge; penumbrae widen with distance
ellipses: minor axis on cylinder axis, rounder farther from eye level

architecture.summary: Floors stacked on walls, openings over openings, every dimension keyed to the body; perspective from a constructed grid; daylight falls off fast with room depth.

key_numbers.window: sill 0.8-0.9 m, head aligned with door head ~2.0-2.1 m (judgement)
key_numbers.daylit_depth: 1.5-2 x window head height (2.5 without blinds) (MIT 4.401, Reinhart)
key_numbers.daylight_factor: <2% inadequately lit, >5% well lit (CIBSE via Wikipedia)

rules: Mass as boxes on the ground plane, then openings on a facade grid, then thickness, then texture (judgement)
Openings stack and align; window heads align with door heads (judgement)
Level gaze keeps verticals vertical; tilt gives one third VP (handprint, OUP)
Each building plane holds one value per light; shadow planes cooler from sky, warmer low from ground bounce (judgement)
Windows seen from outside in daylight are darker than the wall unless reflecting sky at grazing angles (Fresnel; judgement)
Sun through a window projects a skewed copy of the window, all patches one direction (geometry)
Room light falls off with depth; window wall darkest from inside (MIT; judgement)
Texture gradient: single bricks only near, courses as tone farther (judgement)
checks: door / standing figure ~1.15-1.2; storey ~1.6-1.8 figures
window heads and sills align and meet the cornice's VPs
verticals all vertical or all converging on one VP3
every opening has a reveal and a sill shadow
interior falloff with distance from window; sun patches consistent
windows from outside darker than wall in daylight, lit at night
bricks only in foreground

objects.summary: Simple solids resting on a table; each material read by how it splits light into specular, diffuse, transmitted and subsurface parts, and by the contrast, sharpness and placement of its highlights.

key_numbers.glass: R0 ~4% per face (8% pane), Brewster ~56 deg, total internal reflection beyond ~42 deg (Wikipedia, Fresnel equations)
key_numbers.gloss_perception: highlight contrast + blurriness explain 69% of perceived gloss in painted grapes; coverage no effect (Di Cicco 2019); satin shininess rises with mean luminance and highlight coverage (Di Cicco 2021)
key_numbers.beurs_grapes: body + shading -> edge reflections -> bloom scumble (dry) -> highlight where no bloom -> glazes -> seeds; highlights~gloss r=0.94, bloom layer~bloom r=0.92 (Di Cicco 2020)
key_numbers.object_sizes_cm: wine glass 15-22, tumbler 9-12, bottle 30, plate 26-28, apple 7-8, grape 1.5-2.5 (judgement)

rules: Non-metals: white (light-coloured) highlight over coloured diffuse body; metals: no diffuse, reflections tinted only for gold/copper/brass (LearnOpenGL)
Everything grows more reflective toward grazing angles (Fresnel)
Rougher = wider, dimmer highlight; smoother = smaller, sharper, brighter (LearnOpenGL)
Highlights must agree with shading and stretch along least curvature, or they read as paint spots (Beck & Prazdny via Todd 2004)
Dark surfaces look glossier; light gloss next to dark looks less glossy (Hansmann-Roth 2017; Motoyoshi 2007)
Glass = refracted background + few reflections + edge lines + caustics; coloured glass darker where thick (Fleming 2011; Beer-Lambert)
Translucent materials (marble, wax, milk, fruit, skin, leaves): soft, colour-bled shadow edges (Jensen 2001)
Velvet: bright silhouette and shadow-edge rims (Koenderink & Pont 2003); satin: many bright highlights (Di Cicco 2021)
Finished wood: shifting subsurface fibre highlight under the finish highlight (Marschner 2005)
scene.py gloss has no Fresnel, transmission or SSS: paint glass, metal and translucency over the blockout
checks: every highlight placed by light and eye, with the light's shape and colour
sharp high-contrast highlights only on glossy things
glass: shifted background, dark+light edge lines, 2-5 reflections, caustic, contact
metal: reflections not local-colour shading
translucent things: warm soft shadow edges and glow
fabric type: satin / velvet / matte read correctly
contact and cast shadows consistent; ellipses from one eye level

animals.summary: Bodies built on one mammalian skeleton with joints lifted off the ground (digitigrade, unguligrade); measured in head lengths; covered by fur, feathers or scales read as masses; moving in real gaits and wingbeats.

horse_withers_height_heads.value: 2.5 (= body length, point of shoulder to buttock)
horse_withers_height_heads.source: Bourgelat canon in Cuyer, Artistic Anatomy of Animals

horse_canon_caveat.value: only 14 of 50 horses surveyed matched 2.5 x 2.5

horse_one_head_lengths.value: neck; girth depth; elbow-fetlock; shoulder-withers; ground-hock; hock-stifle

horse_landmarks.value: hock level with the chestnuts; elbow and stifle level; point of buttock slightly above shoulder joint

joint_names.value: stifle = knee; hock = ankle; horse 'knee' = wrist; fetlock = knuckle
joint_names.source: Lawson, Anatomy and Physiology of Animals

stances.value: plantigrade (human, bear), digitigrade (dog, cat, most birds), unguligrade (horse, cattle, deer, pig)
stances.source: UMN veterinary anatomy; Line of Action

dog_body_length_vs_withers.value: about equal for a medium dog; varies widely by breed

cat.value: body longer than tall; tail about body length; shoulder blades rise when walking

cattle.value: shorter legs and neck than a horse, hump over shoulder, wide chest, dewlap, cloven hooves, horizontal pupils

horse_gaits.value: walk 4-beat ~7 km/h never airborne; trot 2-beat diagonal ~13 km/h; canter 3-beat 16-27 km/h; gallop 4-beat 40-48 km/h, airborne with legs gathered under the body

bird_feathers.value: primaries 9-11 (passerines 10) on the hand; secondaries 6-40 on the forearm; tail 12 (6 pairs); alula on the thumb

wingbeat.value: downstroke gives most thrust; upstroke wing partly folded, primaries open; hummingbird ~43 Hz

fish_fins.value: pectoral, pelvic, anal, dorsal, caudal, adipose (trout, salmon, catfish); lateral line along flank

insects.value: head, thorax, abdomen; 3 leg pairs all on the thorax; usually 2 wing pairs on thorax segments 2-3

countershading.value: darker back, lighter belly cancels top-light shading; model the form through it

fur.value: masses of value and colour following growth direction; detail only where light meets dark

checks: Main animal measured in head lengths: horse withers height and body length ~2.5 heads (flag outside 2-3)
Each leg matches a real gait phase; a galloping horse in the air has its legs gathered under the body
Joints in place: the high 'backward' joint on dogs, cats and birds is the ankle; elbow and stifle level on a horse
Fur and feathers as value masses following growth; texture only at light-dark edges and silhouette
Form modelled through countershading: back and belly still read as lit and shadowed planes
Bird in flight: separated primaries and a believable stroke phase; at rest: wings folded into the body line
At a distance the animal reads from its silhouette alone
avoid: flying gallop (all legs extended in the air)
toy proportions or puppy heads on adults
all four legs vertical and symmetric

trees-plants.summary: Branching structures that conserve cross-section (Leonardo's rule), read as a few clumped masses with sky holes; the darkest upright plane in a sunlit landscape; colour set by species and season.

leonardo_rule.value: sum of daughter branch cross-sections = parent (exponent ~2, measured 1.8-2.3)

branch_count_scaling.value: halving branch radius ~ four times as many branches

crown_types.value: excurrent: one leader, conical (most conifers); decurrent: no clear leader, spreading (most broadleaves)

carlson_value_order.value: sky > flat ground > slopes > uprights (trees darkest) in sunlight; compressed in mist; snow may reverse

autumn_colour.value: yellow = carotenoids left; red = anthocyanins made before leaf fall; orange = both; brown = anthocyanin + chlorophyll

distance.value: twigs become a mist; thin stalks and leaves vanish leaving a vague darkness

sky_holes.value: varied, slightly darker than open sky

checks: At each fork the daughters together look as thick as the parent; branches taper outward
Crown in 3-5 value masses with lit and shadow sides; outline broken by clumps and sky holes
Sky holes exist, vary in size, slightly darker than open sky
In sun, trees are the darkest plane unless snow, backlight or mist explains otherwise
Species and season read: conical with a leader or spreading; leaf colour fits the season
Detail only at silhouettes and in the light; interiors and distant trees as masses
Tree casts a shadow that follows the ground
avoid: every leaf painted at middle distance
uniform dab texture over the crown
trees floating without root flare or shadow

flowers.summary: Whorls of modified leaves with species-specific part counts and symmetry, built on simple solids whose openings are ellipses in perspective; translucent petals; fruit as solids with distinct skins.

whorls.value: sepals, petals, stamens, carpels from outside in

part_counts.value: threes (monocots: lily, tulip, iris); fours or fives (most eudicots)

symmetry.value: radial (daisy, rose) or bilateral (orchid, pea, snapdragon)

golden_angle_deg.value: 137.5; ~92% of spiral plants show Fibonacci phyllotaxis

sunflower_spirals.value: e.g. 34/55; 74% of 768 counted spiral families Fibonacci

perspective.value: turned flowers are ellipses; flat flower centre stays mid-ellipse, cone flower centre drops as it turns

solids.source: circle and cone: CNPS; rest judgement

fruit_bloom.value: wax on grape, plum, blueberry: whitish dull coating

still_life_light.value: one directional light from the side models each bloom

dutch_bouquets.value: assembled from separate studies, mixing seasons; few painted from life

checks: Petal count and symmetry fit the species
Every turned bloom sits on an ellipse whose minor axis follows the stem; stems enter the centre
Blooms face several directions; at least one in profile or from behind
Each bloom modelled as one form first; petals inside a cup in shadow
Skins differ: glossy sharp highlight, waxy soft bloom, velvet soft rim
Detail and hard edges concentrated at the focal bloom; some edges lost
avoid: clip-art five-petal flowers all facing front
pure white flowers with grey shadows

landscape.summary: Ground as planes by angle to the sky (Carlson), built by layered and fractured rock, receding by linear perspective, texture gradient and aerial perspective.

rock.value: layered, constant layer thickness across an outcrop; fractures set block edges; weathering rounds edges; smooth vertical cliffs rare

rock_weathering_colour.value: dark rock lightens, light rock darkens with exposure

angle_of_repose_deg.value: dry sand 34, wet sand/crushed stone 45, sandy gravel 25-30, snow 38

scree.value: usually below angle of repose, concave, largest blocks at the base

aerial_perspective.value: lighter (dark things), bluer, lower contrast, less detail with distance; Leonardo: five times as far, five times bluer

texture_gradient.value: texture finer and smoother with distance

cloud_shadows.value: overhead cover most ground; distant ones linear and horizontal

converging_lines.value: rows, furrows, path edges on level ground meet on the horizon

checks: Squint: sky lightest, flat ground, slopes, uprights darkest (unless snow, backlight or mist)
Each step back lighter, bluer, lower contrast, softer
Converging lines on level ground meet on the horizon
Rock shows layers and fracture planes with varied block sizes; loose slopes no steeper than ~35-40 deg, concave
Texture size decreases steadily with distance
Cast and cloud shadows follow the ground's undulations
avoid: ground standing up like a wall
paths as ribbons straight up hills
plane values out of order without reason

water.summary: A surface that mixes reflection (rising from ~2% looking down to ~100% at grazing), transparency and disturbance; reflections follow the inverted-world law and are stretched vertically by ripples.

reflection_law.value: reflection = the world inverted below the water level, seen in true perspective from the eye: verticals straight down, lengths from water level, undersides visible

fresnel.value: ~2% reflected looking straight down, ~100% at grazing

look_down_vs_along.value: down: see into the water; along: see reflections

reflection_values.value: light things reflect a little darker; dark things a little lighter

ripples.value: distant: images stretched vertically; near: broken horizontally; verticals stay decisive, horizontals diffuse

glitter_path.value: length 4 x max wave slope (high sun); width/length = sin(sun elevation); smooth water = one glint

wave_breaking.value: crest no sharper than ~120 deg; breaks when front face passes vertical

beaufort.value: 0 mirror; 1 scaly ripples; 3 crests begin to break; 4 white horses; 6 whitecaps and spray; 7 foam streaks; 8 spindrift; 10-12 sea white

water_colour.value: blue only through several metres; green = algae; brown = tannins; coloured water tints reflections of dark things
water_colour.source: WebExhibits; Wikipedia, Color of water; Ruskin

transmitted_light.value: thin wave crests glow green, most saturated colour

rain.value: large drops ~10 m/s; read as streaks

checks: Verticals reflect straight down; lengths from water level under the object; set-back objects' reflections shorter or hidden
Light things reflect slightly darker, dark things slightly lighter; no pure black or white reflection
Near water shows body colour or bottom; far water mirrors the sky and matches its value at the horizon
Ripples stretch reflections vertically far away and break them horizontally near
Glitter path long and narrow for a low sun, on the sun-viewer line
Wave scale, whitecaps and spray agree with one Beaufort force and the picture's wind
Transmitted light at crests is the most saturated water colour; foam broken, never an outline
avoid: reflection as flipped copy of the picture
uniform water colour to the horizon

sky.summary: A light source gradating toward the horizon and away from the sun, carrying clouds at WMO levels in perspective, with fixed optical geometry (sun and moon 0.5 deg, rainbow 42 deg, halo 22 deg).

clear_sky_gradient.value: lighter and whiter toward the horizon; darker, more saturated away from the sun; dull warm glare near the sun; darkest ~65 deg from the sun (zenith at sunrise/sunset); >=4 mixtures

cloud_levels_temperate_km.value: high 5-13 (Ci, Cc, Cs); middle 2-7 (Ac, As, Ns); low 0-2 (St, Sc, Cu, Cb)

cumulus.value: sharp outlines, cauliflower tops, brilliant white sunlit parts, dark nearly horizontal base

cumulonimbus.value: towering, flattened fibrous anvil top, very dark base, virga

clouds_in_perspective.value: common base height; smaller, flatter, closer together toward horizon

cloud_shading.value: keep shadow sides lighter than measured: cloud light is unattainable in paint

rainbow.value: radius 42 deg around antisolar point, red outside, darker sky outside

halo.value: 22 deg around the sun, red inner edge; sun dogs 22 deg each side

twilight_deg_below_horizon.value: civil 0-6, nautical 6-12, astronomical 12-18; Belt of Venus 10-20 deg above antisolar horizon over Earth's shadow

coloured_clouds.value: sunset colours mostly on cirrus and altocumulus

checks: Clear sky darker and more saturated away from the sun, lighter toward the horizon; lighter, warmer, duller near the sun
Low clouds share a base and shrink, flatten and crowd toward the horizon; tops brightest, bases grey, shadow sides light
Cloud types at their WMO levels, one wind, one weather
Sun and moon ~0.5 deg of the field of view; moon's lit side faces the sun
Rainbow 42 deg around antisolar point red outside; halo 22 deg; rays converge on sun or antisolar point
Ground light colour, shadow colour and contrast match the sky's hour and weather
avoid: clouds too dark on a sunny day
giant sun or moon as observation

fire-smoke.summary: Flames as soot glowing at 1,100-1,400 C, shaped by buoyancy into a steady base and flickering tongues; a light source with inverse-square fall-off; smoke whose colour depends on light direction and particle size; steam visible only after it condenses.

candle_zones.value: dark vapour core at wick, yellow soot-incandescent middle, blue base; ~1100 C, hot spots 1300-1400 C

incandescence_colour_C.value: visible red ~525; dull red ~700; cherry 800-900; orange 1000-1200; yellow ~1100-1250; white 1300+

fire_zones.value: continuous flame to 0.08 Q^0.4 m; intermittent to 0.20 Q^0.4 m; buoyant plume above (Q in kW; 33 kW: 0.3 m, 0.8 m)

flicker_hz.value: f ~ 1.5/sqrt(d m): ~10 Hz at 2 cm, ~1.5 Hz at 1 m

plume.value: laminar near source, turbulent higher as it speeds up

smoke_colour.value: blue with light behind viewer; yellow-brown against bright sky; white when moist; grey-black when sooty

steam.value: clear gap at the spout is the steam; the white cloud is condensed droplets

falloff.value: inverse square: twice the distance, a quarter of the light

checks: Flame runs near-white core, yellow, orange, red tips; darker zone at a candle wick
Firelight pool is small and falls off by inverse square
Flames: continuous base with broken detached tongues above
Smoke smooth near source, turbulent higher; colour fits background and light direction
Steam has a clear gap at the spout and fades
Flame, smoke and steam lean with the picture's wind
avoid: icon teardrop flames with hard outline
dark red at the hottest centre
one candle lighting a whole room evenly
smoke as grey cotton or a solid tube

face.summary: A ball (cranium) with a face of big planes on it; features as small planes in the light; expressions are whole-face patterns of action units.

thirds.value: hairline-brow, brow-nose base, nose base-chin equal; hairline halfway between brow and crown

planes.value: front, side and bottom planes; brow, socket, cheekbone corner, nose wedge, muzzle, jaw underside

values.value: light, 2-3 halftones, shadow; one value per plane

laugh.value: AU6+12+25+26 (+10), intense laughter may add AU4; joy follows AU6

surprise.value: AU1+2+5B+26; brows curved, mouth loose and open

fear.value: AU1+2+4+5+7+20+26; brows level, upper lid higher, lips stretched

checks: Squint: 3-5 value shapes (light front, shadow side, socket, under-nose, under-jaw) read as a head before any feature
Name the expression's AUs and see each one; a laugh needs lifted cheeks and narrowed eyes, not only an open mouth
Cover the mouth, then the eyes: each half still says the feeling
No feature outlined; eyes are lit spheres under lids
No two faces built on the same proportions
Head thrown back from below hides the face: turn it or move the eye
avoid: emoticon or mask with drawn features

figure.summary: A gesture through the whole body, three masses (head, ribcage, pelvis) tilting against each other, weight landing on a support, limbs that overlap and shorten as they turn.

midpoint.value: the greater trochanters, just above the pubic arch

legs.value: 3.5-4 heads floor to crotch; arms about 3 heads

heads_by_age.value: birth 4, age 5 about 6 (USF) or 5.5 (Tuts+), 7-9 about 6, teens 6.5-7, adult 7.5
heads_by_age.source: USF head to height; Tuts+ drawing different ages

sex.value: hip:shoulder circumference 1:1.03 women, 1:1.18 men; waist-hip 0.67-0.80 in art

line_of_action.value: one C, S or straight line through the spine; more curve, more force

contrapposto.value: weight on one foot, shoulders and hips tilt opposite

balance.value: centre of gravity over the support or held by a visible force

foreshortening.value: receding forms shorten, shrink and overlap

checks: One clear line of action through the figure
Shoulder line and hip line tilt against each other in a weight-bearing pose
Centre of gravity over the support, or a force you can see
Measure in heads for the age; fingertips at mid-thigh
Forms turned to the eye overlap and shorten
Figures in a group lean toward or away from each other

hands-feet.summary: A palm block, fingers of three stacked cylinders on a curved knuckle row, a thumb that starts at the wrist and bends across the palm; the foot a wedge with an arch.

construction.value: palm as a flat 'steak', fingers as stacks of three cylinders; knuckles on concentric arcs

thumb.value: moves from low at the wrist; max 90 deg from little finger; spread 1.5 index lengths

foot.value: about one head long; wedge with inner arch

checks: Hand about a face long
Palm block, then fingers, then the thumb as its own wedge from the wrist
Knuckles on an arc
A hand on something makes contact (shadow, fingers following the surface)
The hand's gesture agrees with face and body
avoid: thumb as a stick from the wrist

sex-age.summary: How a painted person reads as female or male, child, adult or old. Ambiguity reads male, so a woman needs positive feminine cues; several moderate cues agreeing beat one exaggerated cue. At thumbnail size only hair, outline (jaw, neck, shoulder-hip, waist), facial contrast and skin colour survive.

male_bias.value: ambiguous bodies and faces are categorised as male, and faster; feminine cues must be present, not just masculine ones absent
male_bias.source: Johnson, Iida and Tassinary 2012, Proc R Soc B (PubMed 23075835)

face_accuracy.value: hair hidden: humans 96%; 12 full-face distances 85%; 16 2-D+3-D measures 94%

face_feature_rank_isolated.value: brows+eyes > brows > eyes > jaw > chin > nose+mouth > mouth; nose alone carries nothing

facial_contrast.value: higher eye/lip-to-skin luminance contrast reads female, lower reads male; can flip an androgynous face; strongest face cue that survives blur
facial_contrast.source: Russell 2009, Perception; 'strongest at blur' is judgement

skin_colour.value: redder skin reads male, greener-yellower female; redder lips read female; beard zone darker in men
skin_colour.source: Dupuis-Roy et al. 2009 (ScienceDaily); Dupuis-Roy and Gosselin 2015 (Medical Xpress)

brow_to_eye.value: larger lid band under the brow in women; important, but less than eye and mouth luminance

moon.summary: A 0.5 deg disc whose lit limb faces the Sun; tiny on any ordinary lens (f/110 mm on the sensor); about as bright as sunlit asphalt, so pale and low-contrast against a day sky and blown out against a night sky.

angular_diameter.value: 29.3-34.1 arcmin (~0.5 deg); fingernail at arm's length

image_size_mm.value: focal length / 110 (f/101-f/117 over the orbit): 24 mm -> 0.22, 50 mm -> 0.45, 200 mm -> 1.8, 400 mm -> 3.6; on a 48 cm-wide sheet from a 24 mm-high frame: 24 mm lens 4.3 mm (22 px), 50 mm 9 mm (45 px)
image_size_mm.source: UniquePhoto Q&A f/110 rule; table derived

lit_limb.value: faces the Sun along the great circle; Northern Hemisphere waxes on the right, Southern on the left
lit_limb.source: Wikipedia, Lunar phase; Trefethen moon tilt

terminator_geometry.value: lit fraction k=(1+cos phase angle)/2; limb a semicircle, terminator a half-ellipse with semi-minor R*|2k-1|; lit width k x diameter

phase_times.value: waxing gibbous rises ~15:00, high ~21:00, in the east in the late afternoon with the Sun in the west; first quarter rises ~12:00; full never in a day sky

surface.value: albedo ~0.12 (worn asphalt); maria darker basalt, 31% of the near side; true colour muted brownish grey; rays from Tycho and Copernicus bright

maria_vs_highlands_Lstar.value: ~50 vs ~80 in the lit half (NASA rendering, approximate)

relief.value: craters in relief only along the terminator; full Moon flat, no shadows; quarter 1/11 as bright as full

day_contrast.value: Moon 1.1-1.7x the sky beside it (under one stop): pale, bluish, faint maria; dark part of the disc equals the sky
day_contrast.source: derived from Wikipedia luminance table (Moon 2.5 kcd/m2, clear sky 7 kcd/m2) and Space.com phase brightness

vs_sunlit_ground.value: about the value of sunlit worn asphalt; darker than sunlit skin, paper or cloud (Looney 11 = one stop under sunny 16)

night_contrast.value: ~10^6 x the night sky; clipped white featureless disc with a glow when the land is exposed (measured: disc L* 99.4, glow L* 30 -> 18 from limb to 2 radii, sky L* 6)
night_contrast.source: Wikipedia luminance table; measured NASA NHQ201611140005

bw_filters.value: yellow darkens blue sky slightly, orange very dark, red almost black; the brownish-grey Moon barely changes, so it stands out
bw_filters.source: Ilford; Photography Mad; judgement for the Moon

low_moon.value: not larger (1.5% farther; perceived ~50% larger); flattened ~5 arcmin (a sixth) by refraction; yellow-orange
low_moon.source: NASA; Wikipedia, Moon illusion; Atmospheric refraction

earthshine.value: lights the dark part of a thin crescent a few days from new, at twilight or night; invisible by day and on a gibbous

Maria as a few soft patches at naked-eye size, in the near side's real pattern
A horizon Moon flattened by a sixth and warm, not enlarged

lit side away from the Sun
full circle outlined behind a crescent or gibbous by day
paper-white day Moon with dark crisp maria

drapery.summary: Cloth carries the weather and the feeling: fewer, bigger folds as broad colour planes in loaded strokes, bellying and streaming with one wind; deep saturated colour; gravity and support points kept.
rules: Cloth carries the weather and the feeling: show wind direction and force before fabric construction (Delacroix, Christ Asleep, Met 29.100.131; Faust lithograph, Met 62.617.1; Martin, CMA 1997.138)
Fewer, bigger folds: one or two fold systems per cloth mass, secondary folds as single strokes, no small wrinkles (observed across Delacroix, Gericault, Martin)
Wind-filled cloth is a convex pocket or sail: lit belly, dark hollow, carried by silhouette; the belly may be exaggerated (judgement, from Christ Asleep and the Faust cape)
Flag folds stream as one long taut tapering shape from the anchor, not many small flutters (Faust cape; Martin shawl)
Colour over line: each cloth plane in one loaded stroke, drawing sacrificed to drama (L'Artiste 1832 via OpenLearn; Smarthistory/McCoy)

Cloth holds the strongest local colour, deep not gay: deep reds and blues against earths and storm greys (Burke II.17: no 'gay or gaudy drapery', 'except perhaps a strong red'; observed Christ Asleep, Rebecca)
Heavy wool hangs plumb in long pipe folds and barely lifts; light cloth (capes, shawls, sails, sheets) shows the wind (Gericault, Return from Russia, CMA 1931.48)
White cloth (sails, laundry, dresses) is the brightest note on the land, still below the sky's brightest (measured: Whalers Met 96.29; Flers CMA 1980.259; Oxbow umbrella Met 08.228)
Edges crisp on the lit belly, lost into the storm on the shadow side; in prints hatching follows the wind (Rebecca Met 03.30; Faust)
At landscape scale a figure's clothing is two or three strokes, one light and one dark shape streaming the same way (Martin, CMA 1997.138)

wind plus gravity gives a diagonal; heavy cloth lifts less than light
windward side presses and reveals the body, leeward side billows
one wind for cloth, hair, grass, smoke and trees
wet cloth darker, heavier, clinging; translucency per layer 1 (no Romantic convention found: judgement)
avoid: many small even wrinkles, stitching or texture inventories
fold lines drawn over flat colour

flags: translucent wet linen: no Romantic convention found; layer 1 governs it

wet linen sheets: big lit bellies with 2-3 fold lines from each peg, heavy sagging bottom edge; the torn-free sheet a twisting flag, leading edge crisp, trailing edge lost in haze (judgement)

face.summary: Individual, psychological faces; passion reaches the face (open mouths allowed); head often lifted to the light; at figure scale three to five value shapes; dramatic side light, warm thick lights, cool thin shadows lost into hair and ground.

rules.rule: Make each face particular (nose, jaw, brow, weathering); keep the classical profile only for allegory.

rules.rule: Expression stronger than neoclassical; the open mouth is allowed; the whole head (tilt, neck strain) carries it.

figure.summary: The body carries a passion and the weather: twisted, off balance, arms flung along the storm's diagonal, heavy observed masses, broken contours, dramatic side light, visible brushwork; against the calm, even-lit, firm-contoured neoclassical ideal.

rules.rule: Push the line of action past life: arms to full stretch, torso twisted against the pelvis, the body on one diagonal that continues the storm, sea or sail.
rules.source: Smarthistory, Raft of the Medusa: https://smarthistory.org/theodore-gericault-raft-of-the-medusa/; Met 436176 Delacroix, Christ Asleep during the Tempest; Met 358057 Gericault, Shipwreck of the Meduse

hair.summary: Hair let loose: unbound, dishevelled or wet as a sign of passion and nature's force; one dark mass with few groups, edge lost into dark ground or weather, a few locks in the light in visible strokes; moves with the same weather as cloth and sky.

rules.rule: Loose, unbound hair belongs to the Romantic figure; in the period's code dishevelled hair signals distraction or distress, so face and pose decide the reading.
rules.source: Showalter 1985, Representing Ophelia (quoted): https://eportfolios.macaulay.cuny.edu/milsteinsandbox/?p=51; CMA 1941.215.13 Delacroix, The Death of Ophelia; Met 334042 Goya, A woman pulling at her hair; Met 438814 Delacroix, The Abduction of Rebecca

rules.rule: Fewer groups than life: one dark mass, two or three big falls, a few locks only where the light catches; no texture in the shadow mass.
rules.source: judgement, observed on CMA 1964.284 Delacroix, Marguerite-Juliette Pierret, Met 438107 Chasseriau, Desdemona, CMA 1941.215.13 Delacroix, The Death of Ophelia

rules.rule: Lose the edge into dark ground on the shadow side and into the weather leeward; find it only against the lit face or light sky.
rules.source: judgement, observed on Met 438107 Chasseriau, Desdemona, CMA 1964.284 Delacroix, Marguerite-Juliette Pierret, Met 436423 Fuseli, Night-Hag

rules.rule: Hair is among the darkest values beside the face so the lit face reads against it.
rules.source: judgement, observed on CMA 1941.215.13 Delacroix, The Death of Ophelia, Met 438107 Chasseriau, Desdemona

rules.rule: Wet hair as dark tapering ropes following water or wind, light gaps between them.
rules.source: CMA 1941.215.13 Delacroix, The Death of Ophelia; layer 1 hair (wet)

rules.rule: Strokes long, tapering, visible, following growth and fall; light a warm band of a few strokes across the locks, not a polished sheen; shadows coloured, not black.

light-shadow.summary: One cloud-break light on a minority of the land; the sky holds the light, storm cloud ~L*30 never black, shadowed land darker than the cloud, lit land below the sky; warm dark earth shadows under storm.
rules: Light a place, not the scene: one cloud-break patch on about 4-26% of the land (median 13%), the rest one connected shadow family (measured, 14 works)
The sky holds the light: most of the brightest pixels above the horizon, sky mean about 20 L* above the land (measured; Constable: sky the 'chief organ of sentiment', Met essay)
The lit land stays below the sky's brightest: about 25 L* lower in storm oils, 2-8 in luminous watercolours (measured)
Storm cloud darks about L* 28-32, never black; the shadowed land is darker than the darkest cloud (L* 5-18) (measured, 5 storm oils)
Light often lands in the middle distance with a dark foreground; keep aerial perspective in the darks, which lift toward the horizon (measured: Branch Hill, Hampstead, Flers, Oxbow)
Storm edge: dark mass on one side, light falling beyond (Met, The Oxbow 08.228; Michel CMA 1975.78; Hampstead CMA 1916.1027)
Quick transition from light to dark is the strongest value step (Burke II.15); on the ground the patch edge stays soft like a cloud shadow, cloud rims crisper (judgement)
Light colour: cool silver-white or warm gold both belong; a cold-white storm light is within the current (measured)
Shadows under storm are warm dark earth, not blue: lit by grey cloud and brown bounce (measured ground darks; judgement for reading, consistent with layer 1)
Visible shafts of light or rain from the cloud break are allowed (Hampstead; Moel Cynwich CMA 2010.147; Oxbow)
Plan three value families: sky, lit patch (below sky), shadowed land (below darkest cloud) (judgement from measurements)
keep: one dominant light; cast shadows and terminators agree with it
light-family / shadow-family rule inside the lit patch, with terminator, core and reflected light
low light gives long raking shadows

aerial perspective in darks and saturation

objects.summary: Everyday objects small, used, weathered and summary: picturesque roughness, uprights against the sky, white things as the land's brightest accents, all bearing the same weather and light.
rules: Everyday objects are small traces of ordinary life inside the vastness, 'a reminder of the reality of the scene' (CMA, Turner Fluelen 1954.129); 'the minute with the infinite' (CMA 2010.147)
Picturesque character: weathered, irregular, rough, mended; 'roughness ... sudden variation ... irregularity'; mossy rough-hewn pales of unequal heights, not neat post-and-rail (Price 1794)
Summarise detail: a few loaded strokes, material shown by one or two lights on the lit side; kept 'at a picturesque distance' (CMA, Constable Branch Hill 1972.48; Flers CMA 1980.259)
Objects bear the weather: they agree with the wind and the single light (Constable, Mill Near Colchester, Met 2007.41; Oxbow umbrella Met 08.228)
Uprights against the sky: posts, masts, mill sails, blasted trees; 'a perpendicular has more force ... than an inclined plane', rugged beats smooth (Burke II.8)
White things (cloth, a white horse, a wall) are the brightest small accents on the land, placed in the light and kept below the sky (measured: Branch Hill, Flers, Oxbow, Mill)
Objects are in use or just left, not arranged as still life (observed: cart loading, linen bleaching, abandoned easel, fallen arms in Rebecca Met 03.30)
Small warm or red accents in the earth-grey land (Branch Hill harness, Flers, Mill sail)
Silhouette crisp against the sky on the lit side, lost into dark ground (Mill; Oxbow)
keep: correct construction: wheel and basket ellipses, post taper and lean, line sag between supports
real scale against the figure (peg about a hand's width, basket 50-70 cm, post about 2 m: judgement)
contact shadows; objects sit on the ground
avoid: new, neat or symmetrical objects (straight painted post, uniform pegs)
detail legible beyond what the light picks out
an object as large or finished as the figure unless it is the subject
flags: object sizes are real-world judgement, not from a Romantic source
case_notes: post: weathered, slightly leaning, silver on the lit face, the one strong vertical against the sky, lost at the base
line: one fine sagging stroke, lost across darks, crisp against light sky; pegs: a few dark notches, one light touch each
basket: low rough wicker lump, one lit side, contact shadow, correct ellipse, holding a pale linen accent
sources: Constable to Fisher 1821, 'old rotten planks, slimy posts' (secondary): https://www.shafe.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/21-08-Romanticism-John-Constable.pdf

rules: Sky is the subject: horizon 0.51-0.83 of the height down (median ~0.57), sky at least half the picture (measured on 12 Met/CMA works, 7 artists)

One storm mass, not a field of clouds: a single dark body over the top or one side, lower edge level or one long diagonal; small clouds only as torn fragments streaming off it (works sample; Cox 1813 'broad masses')
Darkest at the top, one bright break low under the cloud edge: break ~25-30 L* lighter than the mass (measured, Constable Harrow, Dahl)
Land darker than any sky: brightest sky band 22-38 L* above the land median in the oils (measured)
Cloud darks are coloured mid-darks (~L* 25-40), never black (measured #544c46, #564e41, #595b5c; style doc)
Colour low-chroma: a 'slate-indigo' storm is indigo greyed with earth; no saturated blue (measured; flags any brief asking for a strong indigo)
Break is silver (cool) or cream (warm), never pure white; cool sky over warm land (Cox 1813)
Rain veils: parallel streaks hanging from the cloud base, leaning with the wind, lighter where they cross the break (works sample; value logic is a judgement call)
Edges: mass lost and wet-in-wet; the torn edge against the break and the lit rims are the hardest edges in the sky
Strokes run with the weather: long horizontal drags for streaming cloud, dragged verticals for rain; impasto only on the lights (Met Constable essay; Tate)
Oil on a warm-dark ground for storms (V&A: Constable's brown ground for a stormy day)

rain falls from the dark base, never from the break

aerial perspective at the horizon

space.summary: Space from a big sky (median horizon 0.55 from top) and horizontal value bands; asymmetric with one cropped dark side; figures either tiny or large at the picture plane; aerial perspective kept in the darks.
rules: Build space from the sky and 3-5 horizontal value bands of land, not from vanishing points (measured: Michel, Hampstead, Hallingdal; Martin)
Sky about half the height or more; median horizon 0.55 from top, range 0.48-0.72 (measured, 12 works); the sky is 'the standard of scale' (Constable 1821)
Asymmetry: one dark mass cut by a side edge, the other side open to the distance (measured 11 of 14; Oxbow storm-left/sun-right, Met 08.228)
Two figure scales: tiny in the landscape branch (2-8% of height) or large near the picture plane, heads against the sky (Gericault CMA 1931.48)
Depth by diagonal sweeps of road, river and slope ('curving arcs ... swirl', Martin CMA 1997.138)
Contrast the minute with the infinite (CMA 2010.147; Burke II.8 on littleness)
Aerial perspective kept in the darks and in cooling toward the horizon, even when the light falls in the middle distance (measured: Oxbow, Branch Hill, Moel Cynwich, Hallingdal)
Little ruled perspective: overlap, size, height in the field and air carry depth (judgement; layer 1 vista-space cues)
keep: one horizon at eye level; figures keyed to it
size diminution and 1/D^2 compression of ground bands
clear overlap, no tangents
Koschmieder contrast loss for darks and saturation
avoid: centred horizon with symmetrical classical wings
ruled grid as the main depth cue
sky under half the height in a storm picture
lone figure from behind as default (Teodor habit)
flags: horizon at 0.75 (sky three-quarters) exceeds every measured work (max 0.72; median 0.55) but is within the current (Constable watercolour 0.71, Gericault ~0.72, Monk by the Sea per style doc): allowed as a stated choice
low viewpoint is the figure branch's device; the landscape panoramas mostly look down from a height (Burke II.8 prefers depth, 'not very positive')
case_notes: low viewpoint belongs to the figure branch: horizon at the figure's knees to hips, figure 50-75% of the height, centre about a third in from one side (judgement from Gericault)
cropped edge on the heavy dark side, opposite the open low distance (measured convention)

trees-plants.scope: grass and low vegetation in wind (first entry); trees in storm noted briefly
rules: Make the wind visible: every blade, reed and tuft leans the same way as the rain and cloud (Leypold, Cox, Martin, Cole, Church)
Grass bank as one dark mass with a ragged top; single blades only at the crest edge against light and in the nearest tufts (Leypold, Cox; Cox 1813 on foreground drawing)
Flattened grass as long, curved, combed drags along the slope; standing tufts as tapered flicks downwind (judgement call from Martin and Cox)
Lights sparse and late: short strokes along the lean on tips facing the break, clustered where the light rakes, never an even scatter (Constable's flecks, Tate; Leypold; Cox)
Watercolour grass lights are scraped, lifted, reserved or added in body colour (Met medium lines: Cox Journey Home, Driving sheep; Martin)
Colour ochre, straw, russet, olive: warm in the light, cool olive-brown between tufts; no saturated green (Cox 1813; measured #a98466, #7b6752, #9b7a5d)
Order: dark mass, then mid-tone strokes in the wind direction, then lights (Cox 1813 method)
Trees in storm lean or are broken, with foliage swept one way, silhouetted against the break (Cole, Church, Leypold, Cox)
keep: blades taper and grow from dark bases
texture shrinks with distance
lights face the light source
branch thickness and sky holes (layer 1) for any tree
avoid: every blade drawn across the bank
even dot texture ('spotting the foreground all over', a contemporary complaint)
grass leaning against the wind shown in the sky

Horizon is a dead-level, crisp, ruled line: the one long hard edge; only rain or mist may cut it (Dahl, Delacroix, Atkins, Cotman)

Far sea darker than the sky just above it: 9-15 L* in daylight works, more under the storm (measured; departs from layer 1's mirror equality; ruffled facets reflect the higher, darker sky, a judgement call)

Exactly one lit band where the break's light touches the sea: horizontal, brightest at the horizon, fading toward the viewer, broken ends; placed by the glitter-path geometry (Dahl, Lucas, Isabey, Cotman)
Lit band made of short horizontal touches: impasto flecks in oil, reserved or scratched paper in watercolour (Dahl; Met Cotman medium line)
No wave shapes on the far strip: only horizontal value bands
Colour low-chroma, near the cloud's, slightly bluer or greener and darker; no saturated blue or turquoise far off (measured #7e8886, #918b7a)
Rain veils cross the strip at the sky's rain angle and soften the horizon locally

lit band under the light source on the line to the viewer, long and narrow for a low light
sea darks agree with the sky above
one wind across sea and sky

rules: Keep true anatomy and species markings; birds are not stylised like figures (Met 36718, 54517, 55733; CMA 1930.192).
Enlarge the birds to fill the sheet; two or three birds can be the whole picture (Met 54517, 36718, 55733).
Each bird is a closed silhouette in fine sumi line; plumage is 2 to 4 flat tones by feather tract (Met 54517, 36718).
Feather detail only as short dark tips or scalloped edges along coverts and primaries; the hawk's back becomes a scale pattern (Met 55733, 54517).
Countershading stays as local colour (pale belly, dark back), never as light (judgement, from the works).
Bokashi may grade a wing or tail fan toward the tips; no other modelling (Met 55733; CMA 1985.314 text on ink tones in plumage).
Eye is a dark dot, optionally ringed; no specular highlight (all works).
Ground is blank paper or one flat tone; no cast shadow (Met 56178, 54517; CMA 1930.192).
Pecking: head below the back line, tail raised, back and folded wings one oval seen slightly from above (Met 56178; CMA 1985.362; general rule judgement).
Group birds as a rhythm of different head turns with space between (Met 54517, 56178; CMA 1985.314 pairs).
Pigeon: no ukiyo-e pigeon print found; transfer the sparrow rules, keep small head, flat iridescent neck patch, two wing bars, pink legs (judgement).
keep: species markings
leg and wing anatomy (ankle, folded wing ends at tail)
relative size of birds
feeding posture
avoid: motion blur in a print (only in sketches, Met 56178)
imitation calligraphy in the empty space

rules: Oblique parallel view from above, from the fukinuki yatai tradition (JAANUS; Met Yamato-e essay); one-point perspective only as the uki-e genre (Met 36669; CMA 1916.1154) or a deliberate borrowing (Met 37321).
Ground is bare paper or one flat tone (Met 54670 paper; Met 36922 measured #908375).
When described, the ground is a line pattern: flagstone grid with faint stipple, parallel planks, tile grid or scallops (Met 54377, 55053, 55222, 55287).
The pattern keeps one scale across the ground; no texture gradient (judgement).
Steps and kerbs as a band of darker flat tone, not shadow (Met 54377).
Roofs seen from above as flat planes of tile pattern, cut by the frame (Met 55287, 55222).
Awning or eave edge as one clean key line with an identical repeated motif, cut by the frame (Met 54670; CMA 1930.211).
Straight-down pavement (judgement; no print looks straight down): flat ground colour, cobbles as a repeated cell in thin line, same size everywhere, no shadow in joints.
keep: construction and repetition (planks, tiles, posts)
kerbs and steps where they belong
how curtains hang from eaves
avoid: cast shadows in joints or under awnings
sunlit and shadow faces on buildings
accidental mix of parallel and converging recession

rules: Still life is the surimono subject: food and small objects made 'large and elegant' (RISD Small Pleasures; Harvard).
Fruit is a flat shape of local colour; roundness only as one soft bokashi grade darker toward the rim (Met 54973 measured #f3d6a9 centre to #e3ad74 edge; Met 54971).
No highlights, reflected light, cast or contact shadows (Met 54727, 54971, 54973).
Fruit edges by the colour itself or a thin line in a darker fruit tone; sumi for hard objects such as knife, dish, basket (judgement from Met 54727, 54971, 54973).
Ground is bare paper or a flat band fading upward (Met 54973 green band #dbd2b1 into paper).
Peel is one continuous ribbon spiralling off the fruit, outside and inside in two flat tones; cut flesh a paler flat area (Met 54973).
Cut citrus as a flat disc with segment lines and pips as marks; peeled segments as flat lobes (Met 54727).
Containers carry flat pattern: blue-and-white dish rim, woven basket as a fine grid (Met 54973; CMA 1949.153, 1943.5).
High oblique view; dishes and boxes with parallel edges (Met 54973, 54832; CMA 1949.153).
Fruit in a crate: repeated rounds with the same grade in overlapping rows as pattern; gaps a flat darker tone (judgement; no ukiyo-e crate found).
keep: fruit shape and colour by species
stem, calyx, segment count
overlap order
peel logic

rules: No form shadow, core shadow, reflected light or highlight; every surface is its local colour (AAM via style doc; all works).
No cast shadows; Western-style shadows are a noted exception (CMA 1930.202), so any use is a deliberate flat hard-edged departure (judgement).
Paper is the lightest value; snow and white light are unprinted paper (Portland; CMA 1985.317).
Distance by flat value steps, e.g. three greys from three blocks (CMA 1948.306), never haze.
Bokashi only as bands at edges: sky top, horizon, ground edge, at most inside a fruit or wing (Met 36922, 55733; Portland).
Dawn: dark blue top band to warm peach horizon (Met 36922 measured #2f4f68 to #edc7a6); figures stay flat.
Winter day: grey top band, grey-green sky, deep blue water, paper snow (Met 55733 measured #595453, #809a9a, #374e6e, #f3e6c7).
Night: dark flat sky, flat moon, figures still in local colour (Met 36669; CMA 1930.202, 1992.73).
Rain as ruled straight lines over the scene (CMA 1942.145).
Flat daylight (judgement): pale warm ground or paper, one bokashi band at most, high warm key; warmth told by band and key, not tinted light.
keep: local darkness and lightness of things
sky colour order at dawn and dusk
weather

rules: Boxes, counters and stalls in oblique parallel projection; receding edges stay parallel (Met 51136, 36922, 54973).
Material is told by flat colour plus a line pattern: weave grid, wood grain, tile scales, textile stripes (Met 36922, 54670, 55222; CMA 1949.153).
No highlights or cast shadows, even on metal and lacquer (all works; metal judgement).
Sumi key line, straight and even, round every made object (all works).
Shop curtains and awnings enter from the frame edge and are cut by it (Met 54670, 55287).
Stripes and checks run straight within each face of the cloth and change direction at folds (Met 36922, 54670; style doc; judgement).
Repeated goods (boxes, tubs, lanterns) become pattern (Met 36669, 51136, 36922).
Carried goods as flat silhouettes with pattern (Met 36922; CMA 1985.315).

Market translation (judgement): crates as oblique pale-wood boxes with ruled slat lines; striped awning in two flat colours with an identical repeated scallop on its hem, cut on two sides; shopping bag as a flat silhouette with key-line handles.
keep: construction (slats, hoops, handles, seams)
count of repeated parts
how a stack rests
how cloth hangs from a rail
avoid: converging perspective mixed with parallel boxes

rules: High oblique viewpoint, 'far beyond that of human scale' (Portland on Met 55733); ground fills most of the picture, horizon high or a sky band at the top (Met 55222, 56508, 36922).
Receding edges parallel on one dominant slant; one-point perspective only as deliberate uki-e borrowing (Met 55222, 54377, 55053 vs 36669, 37321; JAANUS).
Verticals stay vertical; no three-point convergence (judgement).
Depth by two or three flat bands, overlap and a jump in scale (Met 55733; CMA 1992.73, 1985.315; Met Yamato-e essay on cloud bands).
Distance by paler, simpler flat tones, never by haze or softer edges (CMA 1948.306; judgement on edges).
One strong diagonal (bridge, deck, road, row of stalls) carries the composition (Met 55433; CMA 1985.318; Met 55222).
Hard crops of near objects at the frame: gates, curtains, roofs, a wing, an oar (Met 36922, 54670, 55287, 55733; CMA 1992.73); far things seldom cut (judgement).
Asymmetry: a large near shape on one side, open space on the other (Met Japonisme essay).
Straight-down view (judgement; no print looks vertically down): the ground becomes the picture plane, pattern undistorted, objects as silhouettes seen from their tops; log it as an extension.
keep: overlap order
relative size of like things at one depth
gravity (verticals vertical)
avoid: accidental mix of parallel and converging lines

rules: Scale jump instead of steady recession: large near figures against a far band of tiny repeated heads, little in between (CMA 1956.753 label: 'People crowding the Ryōgoku Bridge'; Met 55624; judgement that it is a rule).
Near figures cut hard by the frame, down to head and shoulders or a back; straight cut, full detail up to it (Met 55222, 55624; Art UK: 'cropping figures').
Dense overlap of distinct shapes: own key line, different flat colour or pattern, pose and facing per figure; no shadows between them (Met 55222, 36922).
Anonymous passers-by as flat silhouettes in a few greys, no features, overlapping (Met 55624).
Crowds hidden behind something: only heads, hats, spears above a bridge crest, wall or palanquin (Met 36922, 55369).
A frieze of travellers along a road, repeated hats and loads making a rhythm (Met 55369, 36521; CMA 1948.306).
Groups of two and three inside the mass (Met 55222, 36922; CMA 1956.753).
Detail falls off in flat steps: near faces and pattern, then flat colour and outline, then one flat value; distance by paler flat greys, not haze (CMA 1948.306 label: three greys; Met 55222, 55624).

Brief: passers-by enter only from the frame edges (a foot and trouser leg, a coat hem, a bag edge), cut straight with full detail to the edge; subordinate by flatness and lower chroma or one grey each; motion by stride and flipped hem along the edge; vary the pieces so they read as many people (judgement; extension of Met 55222, 55624).
keep: group structure (pairs, threes)
overlap order
one ground plane for the feet
size of like things at one depth
walking direction
avoid: blur, haze or fading toward the frame edge
a steady perspective recession of figures
passers-by competing with the main figure in chroma or pattern

rules: Each garment is one flat colour area inside a long, smooth key-line contour, heavier than the face's lines (Met 55810, 54869, 37176; CMA 1956.753).
Folds are a few lines from support points running with the fall, ending in a taper or small hook, drawn over the pattern; no shading (Met 55810; CMA 1956.753).
White or plain cloth: folds by blind embossing plus a few lines (CMA 1985.309 label); with no embossing in the engine, lines alone (judgement).
Pattern lies flat: motifs keep one size and shape across folds and turns, crests stay circles, flowers run straight through folds (Met 55810, 55800; CMA 1956.753; Met 55185 Western dress).
Motifs are cut by the outline, overlapping cloth and fold lines, never wrapped round the form (Met 55185, 37176, 55810).

Stripes and checks keep constant spacing: straight within a panel and changing angle at a turn (Met 36922, 55222), or bending gently along a large panel's main fall (Met 55810); never compressed or shaded.
Pattern as its own flat colour or paper reserve on the garment's ground (Met 55800; CMA 1956.753; judgement on block logic).
Layered edges (hem, sleeve, collar) as parallel bands of flat colour, each with its own key line (Met 55800; CMA 1985.309).

Patterned shirt: flat ground, pattern at one motif size over the whole shirt, cut by outline, collar, seams and the apron's edge; fold lines at elbow, armpit and waist over it (judgement applying the pattern rule; Met 55185, 55182).

Apron: a separate flat panel in its own colour with its own contour, overlapping shirt and trousers; ties as key-line loops like obi bows; one or two sag lines over the lap (Met 55800, CMA 1985.309 bows; judgement for the apron).

Seated trousers: flat colour per leg area; knee told by the outline's angle; two or three short compression lines behind the knee and at the groin, one or two long lines down the shin (Met 36922, 36521, 55182; judgement for the seated case).
keep: support points and direction of fall
overlap order of garments
where cloth bunches (inside a bent knee or elbow)
few big folds over small ones
material told by the contour: soft cloth sags in long curves, stiff cloth breaks at angles
avoid: pattern foreshortened, compressed or shaded round the form
fold lines that interrupt or hide the pattern instead of lying over it
a soft, painterly hem or contour

rules: The face is one flat area, paper white or one pale flat tint; no planes, socket shadows, cheek or jaw modelling (Met 54869, 55222; CMA 1956.753; NGV essay).
Features are a few very fine key lines, the finest in the print, thinner than garment outlines (JAANUS kashirabori: nose line carved 'much narrower' than drawn; Met 54869).

Ideal type (young men and women): slit eyes, long fine nose ending in a hook, tiny mouth about 0.6-0.8 of one eye's length (hikime kagibana, Wikipedia/JAANUS; read by eye on CMA 1956.753, Met 54869, 55810).

Commoners and working men: same flat face and line, but blunter marks: short thick brow strokes, dash or arc eyes, hook or bulb nose, a wider mouth line that can grin or frown; individuality from skull, jaw and two or three marks (Met 55222, 36922, 36521; CMA 1930.190; judgement that it is a convention).
Old age: add a few key lines (crow's-feet, brow furrow, nose-to-mouth line); grey hair and beard as fine parallel lines (Met 54339).

Closed eyes: one relaxed, downward-sagging arc each, at most a short crease line above; no lashes, no lid shadow (Japanese Wiki Corpus: closed eyes 'as narrow lines'; Met 55800, 55810, 54339; CMA 1985.309).
A sleeper's faint smile lives only in the mouth line: corners tick up by a hair, lips may part slightly; cheeks do not rise (Met 55810; judgement on the limit).
Viewpoints: three-quarter or profile; full front is rare (Wikipedia: 'only two main viewpoints'; judgement from works seen).
Head seen from above or tipped: the skull shape grows and features crowd toward the chin, but each feature keeps its frontal glyph; nostrils and lid planes are not foreshortened (Met 55222).

Brief case, face tipped back and seen from above: turn the head slightly so the face reads three-quarter, keep the glyphs whole, show the tip through the outline (chin and jaw line uppermost, throat as one or two lines) (judgement; log as an extension).

Flesh: paper or one pale warm tint, flat and the same on face and limbs; labourers may take a stronger ruddy tint (Met 36922, 36521); no rosy cheeks (Meiji face bokashi, Met 55182, is a late exception).
Shaved or stubbled skin: a flat pale grey or blue-grey tint (Met 55222, 36922).
Red only as an accent: lower lip, sometimes the eye corner; for a man, the mouth a sumi or dull red line (Met 54869; CMA 1985.309; judgement for men).
keep: oval of the face and the order of features on it (eyes near the half line, mouth nearer the nose than the chin)
turn and tilt of the head
hair overlapping forehead and ears
legible expression
avoid: plane or tonal modelling of the face
outlined, lashed or shaded eyes; iris highlights
a broad grin with raised cheeks on a sleeper
likeness of a real person, including actor likeness (nigao-e)

rules: Proportion follows a type: refined figures long and slight (Utamaro about 8 heads crown to chin, read by eye on CMA 1956.753; Kiyonaga 'exceptionally tall', Harunobu 'child-like': viewingjapaneseprints, Wikipedia), working men compact at about 6-6.5 heads with large heads and sturdy legs (Met 36922 by eye; Met 36521, 55222).
A contemporary ordinary man: use the compact commoner type, about 6.5 heads, the same for every figure of that type (judgement).
The garment's outline is the figure's outline; torso and thighs are located by sleeve, lap and hem, not drawn as anatomy (Met 55810, 54869; CMA 1956.753).
One long contour (nape, back, lap) carries the line of action (Met 55810; CMA 1930.190).
No modelling of masses; folds may be told by blind embossing instead of shade (CMA 1985.309 label).
Bare limbs: a hook for the knee, a bulge in the calf's outline, a tick for the ankle, on flat skin tint (Met 36922, 36521).
Grounded by overlap of body over floor line, mat or bench; no contact or cast shadow (Met 55800; CMA 1985.322).
Sleepers are slack and folded: head dropped, shoulders rounded, arms loose or pillowing the head; long sagging curves (Met 55800, 55810, 54339; CMA 1985.309).
Seated figures read as a mound of cloth with a broad base and one curve for the back (Met 55810; CMA 1985.322).

High view: the floor tilts up on parallel diagonals; the figure is a raised three-quarter view, compressed by overlap, with near limbs not enlarged (Met 55800, 55222; CMA 1985.322; JAANUS fukinuki yatai; judgement on scaling).
Straight-down view: an extension, not a convention; the figure as a flat silhouette seen from its top, parts told apart by overlap and garment colour (judgement, as in ukiyo-e--space).
keep: line of action and the tilts of head, shoulders and hips
overlap order
where the weight rests
relative limb lengths within one figure
avoid: perspective scaling of near limbs (giant near knee or foot)
contact or cast shadows under the body
different canons for figures of the same type
anatomy warped beyond the type into caricature

rules: The mass is flat solid sumi black (flat grey for grey hair) with no highlight band or ring (Met 54869, 55800, 55810; CMA 1956.753).
Against background or clothing the mass has a clean hard contour (all works seen).

Where hair meets skin: a kewari fringe of very fine parallel lines, each strand cut separately and tapering into the face's paper (Waraku: lines 'less than a millimeter in width'; JAANUS kashirabori: hair the hardest part, cut by the master).
Fringe measured on Met 55800: lines about 0.15-0.2 mm wide, 0.5-0.8 mm apart, 1-3 mm long, roughly 1/15-1/20 of the face's length apart (rough reading).
Fringe lines follow growth direction: back and up from forehead and temples, down at sideburns and nape, parallel within a patch, fanning round the head (Met 55800, 55810, 55222; CMA 1985.309).
Short haircut: a black cap with a clean outer contour, kewari fringe at forehead and temples, a few lighter or reserved lines inside for lock direction (Met 55182, 55185).
Grey or thinning hair and beards: fine lines only, paper or skin showing between (Met 54339).
Shaved or stubbled skin: a flat pale grey or blue-grey tint, not lines (Met 55222, 36922).

Short hair from straight above: flat black shape filling the head's top, outer contour a little outside the skull, fine direction lines radiating from the crown whorl, parting as a thin line of skin tint, forehead hairline as a kewari fringe facing the viewer (judgement; log as an extension).
keep: hair shell outside the skull's outline
growth directions radiating from the crown whorl
hairline framing the face's upper third
ears below and in front of the side hair
avoid: highlights or sheen of any kind
soft blurred edges made by blending
strand-by-strand rendering of the whole mass
a hard line drawn between hair and forehead instead of a fringe

rules: Hands small, about 0.5 of the face's length; feet about 0.7 of a head (read by eye on CMA 1956.753, 1985.309; Met 55810, 36922).
Outline only: knuckles and toes as small hooks and lobes; no shading, nails, tendons or dark finger gaps (all works seen).
Refined hands: slender separated fingers, tips curling back (Met 55810, 54869; CMA 1956.753).
Working hands: blunt, mitten-like, two or three finger lines, a knuckle hook on a grip (Met 36922, 55222).
Hands often half hidden in a sleeve or holding an object through it, only fingertips showing (Met 37163).
A held fruit is a flat colour shape with a key-line contour and at most one internal line; curled fingers overlap it, a sliver of fruit between them (Met 37163 crystal ball; judgement for fruit).
A sleeper's grip is loose: fruit resting in a cupped palm on the lap, fingers part-open (judgement, after Met 55800, 55810).
Bare feet: small outline, toes as a fan of lobes, big toe set apart by one line, ankle tick, heel curve (CMA 1985.309; Met 55800, 36922, 36521).

Sandals: sole as a flat band, straps as two or three lines (Met 36922, 36521, 55222); modern shoes as a flat dark shape with sole line and laces or buttons as short lines and dots, no sheen (Met 55185 boots; judgement that it transfers).
Feet at the frame: cut by a straight edge with full detail up to it, one or two sliced mid-foot or at the ankle (crop rule from Met 55222, 55624; judgement for feet alone).
keep: five fingers and toes, thumb opposition, grip direction
joint bending order
big toe on the inside; inner ankle bone higher
avoid: life-size hands (as long as the face)
core shadows on fingers, nails, tendons
feet fading or softening toward the frame edge

rules: Keep layer 1's structure (families, core, reflected light, occlusion); colour becomes value (Skillshare: edges are changes in value)
Sun vs open shade is four stops at noon (sunny 16: f/16 vs f/4); a low sun about 2-3 stops (Wikipedia Sunny 16; judgement)
The filter darkens the blue-skylit shadows and keeps warm sunlit skin light: about one stop more separation than the eye sees (Ilford; Photography Mad; derived, amount judgement)

Values on a sunlit hand: lit L* 75-88, halftones 55-70, shadow family 30-45, core 25-32, contact accents 18-28 in carbon; paper white only for true speculars (photographic ruler; Skillshare 'highlights aren't pure white'; judgement)

FLAG 'soft penumbras': penumbra = distance/110; on the hand (1-3 cm) 0.08-0.25 mm on the sheet, i.e. crisp; softness comes from rounded terminators and depth-of-field blur, not from cast shadows on the hand (layer 1, derived)
Terminators on round forms are gradients, never a soft line (calibration test egg)
Skylit shadow planes facing up lighter than those facing down; reflected light below the darkest halftone (layer 1; judgement)
Crisp family edges by clipped blending; dark-on-dark edges sharpened with a hard pencil or precision_eraser seek (calibration limit 3)
keep: one sun for every shadow and the Moon's lit limb
families separate in value
core, reflected light, occlusion order
cast shadows sharp at contact, softer with distance
avoid: soft cast shadows on the hand under direct sun

Filtered B&W: orange/red filter darkens the blue sky, the brownish-grey Moon keeps its value: Moon 15-30 L* above the sky beside it; suggested sky L* 45-55, highlands L* 70-80 (Ilford; judgement)

Lit limb the hardest edge on the disc; terminator a soft half-ellipse (2-4 px at 22 px); unlit part exactly the sky value, no circle outline, no earthshine, no halo by day (layer 1; judgement)
Two or three soft maria 4-8 L* darker than the highlands; no craters at this size (judgement)

rules: Hue becomes value through the filter: yellow darkens blue sky slightly, orange very dark, red almost black; the filter steepens the vertical gradient (zenith falls more than the hazy horizon) (Ilford; Photography Mad; judgement for steepening)
Gradient: horizon L* 70-80, at the Moon's height L* 45-55, top of frame L* 35-45; side away from the Sun darker (layer 1 gradients; values judgement)

FLAG: a red-filter near-black sky is beyond graphite over a large area (graphite area ~L* 42 and shiny, carbon ~L* 32): draw an orange-filter sky with carbon over graphite at the top (calibration; Vitruvian Studio)
No texture, no banding: a photographic sky has grain ~0; keep 0.5-5 mm mottle at the reference's and the vertical profile monotonic (calibration flat tone and ramp residual 0.44 L*)

Technique: pressure falling toward the horizon, crossed second layer, loose graphite rubbed in, tortillon, paper towel, soft brush; 'draw the sky darker than it looks' (Empty Easel); light layers, blend in stages, no overblending (Vitruvian; Wildlife Art Store)

Cirrus lifted, not drawn: kneaded strokes along one wind, a few fibres with the battery eraser at its smallest, softened; 5-15 L* above the sky; no stylus grooves (WMO via layer 1; Wildlife Art Store white lines; judgement)
The sky has no edges except cirrus fibres, the Moon's limb and silhouettes against it (judgement)

cirrus at WMO height, one wind, perspective toward the horizon

avoid: edges or outlines in the clear sky

Blur grows continuously with each object's distance; no uniform blur field, no cut-out subject (Eclectic Light on Renoir; Wikipedia DOF)
Blur is an edge width, not a value change: blurred things keep their value; thin things narrower than their blur fade to translucent grey (judgement; derived)

drapery.summary: Layer 1's fold logic with the photograph's values: white cotton as light as the lightest skin, its deep valleys nearly black, matte with no specular; in focus a fine regular weave, seams, wear and frayed threads; out of focus only the fold values.

rules.rule: Lit white cotton is as light as the lightest skin (photograph p99.9 L* 83.5); deep fold valleys reach near black (p5 L* 17).
rules.source: LoC FSA/OWI 2017762300 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762300/

rules.rule: Shadows on white fabric are at least a middle grey; reflected light about two steps below the highlights.
rules.source: Skillshare, Shading Folds of Fabric with Graphite Pencil (class notes): https://www.skillshare.com/en/classes/shading-folds-of-fabric-with-graphite-pencil-how-to-get-a-realistic-effect/2141936883

rules.rule: Cotton is matte: no specular streaks; the lightest values are broad lit planes, halftones broad and soft.
rules.source: docs/subjects/drapery.md section 3; judgement from LoC FSA/OWI 2017762300 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762300/

rules.rule: In focus the weave is a fine regular, directional texture (work cotton period 0.8 mm, a clear FFT peak skin lacks); draw it at its spacing and direction, then blend lightly so the period survives.
rules.source: LoC FSA/OWI 2017762300 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762300/; judgement for the method

rules.rule: Seams as small ridges with tiny reserved stitch lights; frayed threads indented or lifted against dark.
rules.source: docs/styles/graphite-hyperrealism.md section 8; judgement

rules.rule: Avoid overusing stumps (muddy flat values); small circular strokes blend without directional edges; blend each fold plane clipped.
rules.source: Skillshare, Shading Folds of Fabric with Graphite Pencil (class notes): https://www.skillshare.com/en/classes/shading-folds-of-fabric-with-graphite-pencil-how-to-get-a-realistic-effect/2141936883; docs/calibration/graphite-hyperrealism.md

rules.rule: Out of focus, weave, seams and soil vanish; fold values and soft fold edges remain.
rules.source: Wikipedia, Depth of field: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_of_field; LoC FSA/OWI 2017762891 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762891/

keep: layer 1 support points, tension, gravity, fold types
creases hard, rolls soft
avoid: pale timid valleys on white cloth
the 1930s work shirt's coarse weave as a target for fine shirting
