face.summary: Layer 1's planes and action units underneath, then what a lens records: skin texture by zone (faint pores, strong folds and stubble), wet eye optics (reserved catchlight, grey sclera, wet rims, clumped lashes), no line anywhere, and focus that grades texture away with distance from the focal plane.

rules.rule: Lay each plane's tone smooth first, then texture inside it with irregular marks; no mirror circles, no outlined spots.
rules.source: Skillshare, How to Draw Skin Texture (class notes): https://www.skillshare.com/en/classes/how-to-draw-skin-texture-realistic-drawing-tips/478193633

rules.rule: Pores are a faint, even stipple near film-grain amplitude (smooth lit skin 1.5-2 L* of 0.25-2 mm texture), never dots that read one by one; pore diameter about 0.2-0.5 mm, 10-90 per cm2.
rules.source: LoC FSA/OWI 2017762300 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762300/; LoC FSA/OWI 2017762891 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762891/; Flament et al. 2015, Facial skin pores, CCID: https://www.dovepress.com/facial-skin-pores-a-multiethnic-study-peer-reviewed-fulltext-article-CCID

rules.rule: Texture by zone: crow's feet and the beard zone carry 2-3 times the texture of smooth cheek or forehead (mid band 4.4-5.1 vs 1.5-2 L*); texture continues at full strength in shadow.
rules.source: LoC FSA/OWI 2017762300 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762300/

rules.rule: A wrinkle is a small valley: a graded dark with a lit lip on one side, not a sharp line; deepest creases about 15 L* below their skin, not black.
rules.source: Skillshare, How to Draw Skin Texture (class notes): https://www.skillshare.com/en/classes/how-to-draw-skin-texture-realistic-drawing-tips/478193633; Wildlife Art Store, create depth: https://www.wildlifeartstore.com/create-depth-in-your-drawing/; LoC FSA/OWI 2017762300 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762300/

rules.rule: Stubble: a grey beard-zone tone first, then short firm marks varying in direction by tract; measured 0.15-0.2 mm wide, 0.5-1.5 mm long, about 0.3 per mm2, at least 11 L* darker than the skin.
rules.source: Skillshare, Drawing Realistic Hair and Beard with Graphite (lesson notes): https://www.skillshare.com/en/classes/drawing-realistic-hair-and-beard-with-graphite/1384601388; LoC FSA/OWI 2017762300 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762300/

rules.rule: Grey hairs in stubble: indent with the stylus before any tone.
rules.source: Skillshare, Drawing Realistic Hair and Beard with Graphite (lesson notes): https://www.skillshare.com/en/classes/drawing-realistic-hair-and-beard-with-graphite/1384601388; docs/styles/graphite-hyperrealism.md section 8

rules.rule: Pupil and lash line are the face's darkest values (photographs L* 3-13): carbon pencil, never burnished 8B.
rules.source: Tuts+, realistic eye: https://design.tutsplus.com/tutorials/how-to-draw-a-realistic-eye--cms-27913; LoC FSA/OWI 2017762300 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762300/; docs/styles/graphite-hyperrealism.md section 4

rules.rule: Reserve the catchlight from the start (indent or never tone it); iris fibres radiate from the pupil and go around it; soft iris edge.
rules.source: Tuts+, realistic eye: https://design.tutsplus.com/tutorials/how-to-draw-a-realistic-eye--cms-27913

rules.rule: One catchlight per open eye, the same source in both, shaped like the source; eyes without catchlights read lifeless.
rules.source: Wikipedia, Catch light: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catch_light

rules.rule: The sclera is grey (about L* 50-70 in sun, darker than lit skin) and shaded as a sphere under the lid; lift only to the reference's value.
rules.source: LoC FSA/OWI 2017762300 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762300/; Tuts+, realistic eye: https://design.tutsplus.com/tutorials/how-to-draw-a-realistic-eye--cms-27913

rules.rule: Lids have thickness; the lower-lid rim and the inner corner are wet with small speculars.
rules.source: Tuts+, realistic eye: https://design.tutsplus.com/tutorials/how-to-draw-a-realistic-eye--cms-27913

rules.rule: Upper lashes 90-160 in up to six rows, longest at the centre, curving down then up, stuck into clumps; at life size they read as a dark band with a few tapered clumps, not an even fringe.
rules.source: Wikipedia, Eyelash: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyelash; Tuts+, realistic eye: https://design.tutsplus.com/tutorials/how-to-draw-a-realistic-eye--cms-27913; judgement from LoC FSA/OWI 2017762300 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762300/

rules.rule: Small sharp speculars on oily zones (nose tip, forehead, lit lip), none on cheek and temple; lifted last with an eraser and seek.
rules.source: judgement; nose-tip p99.9 L* 80.6 from LoC FSA/OWI 2017762300 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762300/

rules.rule: No outline anywhere: every feature edge is two tones meeting.
rules.source: Proko community, Making realistic faces: https://proko.com/community/topics/making-realistic-faces; docs/styles/graphite-hyperrealism.md section 6

rules.rule: Hard edges only in the focal plane; blur grows gradually with distance from it and removes pores, single hairs and lash clumps first while keeping values and the expression.
rules.source: Wikipedia, Depth of field: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_of_field; Wildlife Art Store, create depth: https://www.wildlifeartstore.com/create-depth-in-your-drawing/; Dessindigo, blur effect: https://dessindigo.com/en/blog/drawing-tutorial/draw-blur-effect; out-of-focus texture 0.6-1.2 L* from LoC FSA/OWI 2017762891 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762891/

rules.rule: Follow the photograph's values, not a tutorial's advice to add contrast.
rules.source: docs/styles/graphite-hyperrealism.md sections 1 and 10; flag against Wildlife Art Store, create depth: https://www.wildlifeartstore.com/create-depth-in-your-drawing/

the photograph's geometry and values
slight asymmetry of the two halves
avoid: overblended plastic skin (also makes the face younger)
pores drawn one by one at equal contrast everywhere
flags: Only two 1936 large-format photographs measured; fine-band skin values are mostly film grain, so the mid band (0.25-2 mm) is the texture measure.
Regional skin sheen is judgement: the measured skin-reflectance paper (Weyrich et al. 2006) was not reachable.
At 5 px/mm life-size stubble is under 1 px: hair-by-hair stubble needs the face drawn at about 1.5-2 x life or larger (judgement).

rules.rule: Keep the lens's perspective: parts near the camera are drawn larger; layer 1 canons hold only for parts at the same distance.
rules.source: Wikipedia, Perspective distortion: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perspective_distortion; docs/styles/graphite-hyperrealism.md section 7

rules.rule: Crop close; let the frame cut forms, but keep one line of action running through the fragment.
rules.source: docs/styles/graphite-hyperrealism.md section 7; judgement

rules.rule: Contact with the ground is the passage's darkest value (carbon), with grass pressed under the body and crossing its edges.
rules.source: docs/subjects/figure.md section 4; judgement

rules.rule: Focus ranks the parts; blur grows gradually with distance from the focal plane and is larger behind it than in front.
rules.source: Wikipedia, Depth of field: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_of_field

rules.rule: No contour lines on the body; anatomy shows as tone only.
rules.source: docs/styles/graphite-hyperrealism.md section 6

a real, unidealised build

hair.summary: In focus: strands after values, light strands indented or lifted. Out of focus (this brief): no strands at all, a dark mass with a soft blurred sheen band, edges melting into the grass, darks in carbon laid first.

rules.rule: In focus: general values first, then thin strokes following the strands, brush blending, darker layers, lifted highlights.
rules.source: Skillshare, Drawing Realistic Hair and Beard with Graphite (lesson notes): https://www.skillshare.com/en/classes/drawing-realistic-hair-and-beard-with-graphite/1384601388

rules.rule: In focus, light strands are indented before tone or lifted with an eraser pen.
rules.source: Skillshare, Drawing Realistic Hair and Beard with Graphite (lesson notes): https://www.skillshare.com/en/classes/drawing-realistic-hair-and-beard-with-graphite/1384601388; Veronica's Art, graphite portrait techniques: https://veronicasart.com/?p=5729; docs/styles/graphite-hyperrealism.md section 8

rules.rule: Out of focus: no strands and no indents; keep the mass, its shadow side and one or two soft sheen bands (out-of-focus structure 0.6-1.2 L*).
rules.source: Dessindigo, blur effect: https://dessindigo.com/en/blog/drawing-tutorial/draw-blur-effect; LoC FSA/OWI 2017762891 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762891/

rules.rule: Edges soften gradually with distance from the focal plane; hair farther away melts wider.
rules.source: Wikipedia, Depth of field: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_of_field; Wildlife Art Store, create depth: https://www.wildlifeartstore.com/create-depth-in-your-drawing/

rules.rule: An out-of-focus glint becomes a soft round disc, never a streak.
rules.source: Wikipedia, Bokeh: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bokeh

rules.rule: Dark hair is near black (photograph median L* 4, lights to 40-54): carbon first, blended lightly; graphite alone stops near L* 40.
rules.source: LoC FSA/OWI 2017762891 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762891/; docs/calibration/graphite-hyperrealism.md What still limits 2

rules.rule: Blend inner tones clipped to the mass with a large brush, but blend across the edge unclipped so it blurs into the ground.
rules.source: docs/calibration/graphite-hyperrealism.md; docs/manual/graphite.md; judgement

keep: layer 1 mass first, silhouette wider than the skull
hairline graded into skin, never outlined
avoid: strands or indented lines in out-of-focus hair
a grey mass where the photograph is near black
flags: Layer 1's 'a handful of strands at the light' is overruled out of focus by the optics: draw none.
sources: Skillshare, Drawing Realistic Hair and Beard with Graphite (lesson notes): https://www.skillshare.com/en/classes/drawing-realistic-hair-and-beard-with-graphite/1384601388
Veronica's Art, graphite portrait techniques: https://veronicasart.com/?p=5729

hands-feet.summary: In the focal plane the hand gets the picture's most surface and sharpest edges: joint creases as valleys pointing to the knuckle, the nail as a glossy plate and cross-contour, straight light tendons and soft meandering veins; layer 1's construction underneath, a hierarchy of values and edges over it.

rules.rule: Put the picture's sharpest edges on the focal-plane hand only; everything else softens with its distance from that plane.
rules.source: Wikipedia, Depth of field: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_of_field; Wildlife Art Store, create depth: https://www.wildlifeartstore.com/create-depth-in-your-drawing/

rules.rule: Backs of fingers carry about 3 times the cheek's texture (mid band 5.3 vs 1.9 L*), concentrated in joint creases whose darks reach shadow values.
rules.source: LoC FSA/OWI 2017762891 (measured): https://www.loc.gov/item/2017762891/

rules.rule: Creases follow the hand's action: distal joint a single straight crease, middle joint a spiral, creases pointing to the knuckle; others secondary and light.
rules.source: Proko, details for realistic hands: https://www.proko.com/lesson/how-to-draw-hands-details-for-realistic-hands

rules.rule: Draw each crease as a valley with a lit lip, darkest inside the joint and fading at both ends.
rules.source: judgement; Wildlife Art Store, create depth: https://www.wildlifeartstore.com/create-depth-in-your-drawing/

rules.rule: The nail follows the finger's cylinder and is a cross-contour; add a specular along its curve, a lighter free edge and a soft cuticle overlap; the free edge is the hardest edge of the hand.
rules.source: Proko, details for realistic hands: https://www.proko.com/lesson/how-to-draw-hands-details-for-realistic-hands; judgement for the surface

rules.rule: Tendons straight and as light as the skin or lighter; veins meander in the hollows, slightly darker; neither outlined.
rules.source: Proko, details for realistic hands: https://www.proko.com/lesson/how-to-draw-hands-details-for-realistic-hands

rules.rule: An extended thumb shows the anatomical snuffbox: two tendon ridges and a triangular hollow on the radial back of the wrist.
rules.source: Wikipedia, Anatomical snuff box: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_snuff_box

rules.rule: Create a hierarchy with values and edges; veins are tertiary; leave out what serves no purpose.
rules.source: Proko, details for realistic hands: https://www.proko.com/lesson/how-to-draw-hands-details-for-realistic-hands

rules.rule: Plan crisp edges as reserved lights or masked (clip) blending; the engine cannot sharpen an edge afterwards.
rules.source: docs/calibration/graphite-hyperrealism.md What still limits 3; judgement

keep: layer 1 palm block, knuckle arc, thumb from the wrist
contact and pressure between fingers
perspective size from the camera distance
avoid: age spots and deep wrinkles on a 45-year-old hand
detail on parts outside the focal plane
flags: Nail surface rules are common observation, not a measured source (judgement).
The edge-width measure was too noisy with film grain to give a number for the hand's sharp edge.

sex-age.summary: Viewed close, surface carries age: overblending makes a man younger and can make him a boy; keep in-focus texture and fine lines, add a few indented grey hairs where focus allows, avoid over-ageing; never trace a real person's photograph (at this fidelity it is a likeness).

rules.rule: Keep skin texture and fine lines at the photographic level in focus; smoothing makes a face younger.
rules.source: docs/subjects/sex-age.md section 4 (Fink and Matts 2008; Burt and Perrett 1995; Porcheron et al. 2013; Panhard et al. 2012)

rules.rule: Grey hairs are reserved white: indent before tone, or lift last with an electric eraser at 2-3 px; mid-forties is a little grey at most.
rules.source: Skillshare, Drawing Realistic Hair and Beard with Graphite (lesson notes): https://www.skillshare.com/en/classes/drawing-realistic-hair-and-beard-with-graphite/1384601388; docs/styles/graphite-hyperrealism.md section 8; docs/subjects/sex-age.md section 4 (Fink and Matts 2008; Burt and Perrett 1995; Porcheron et al. 2013; Panhard et al. 2012)

rules.rule: Put the grey where the focus can carry it (stubble near the focal plane); out-of-focus hair cannot show single grey hairs.
rules.source: judgement from Wikipedia, Depth of field: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_of_field

rules.rule: Expression folds (crow's feet, nasolabial fold) crisp; age-only folds (jowls, marionette lines, neck bands, age spots) absent or faint for mid-forties.
rules.source: docs/subjects/sex-age.md sections 4 and 6; judgement

rules.rule: Male cues from structure: brow ridge, jaw angle, thick neck, beard-zone tone and stubble; moderate eye and lip contrast.
rules.source: docs/subjects/sex-age.md sections 1 and 5

rules.rule: Pore size grows from the youngest group and plateaus from about 40: a mid-forties face has visible fine texture on cheek and nose.
rules.source: Flament et al. 2015, Facial skin pores, CCID: https://www.dovepress.com/facial-skin-pores-a-multiethnic-study-peer-reviewed-fulltext-article-CCID

rules.rule: The reference is a rendered or invented face, varied from the studio's defaults; never a traced photograph of a real person, no identifying marks.
rules.source: AGENTS.md rule 5; docs/styles/graphite-hyperrealism.md section 6; judgement
